requirements.requirement: Repair bin/copy-image so a copy preserves source.img's logical length and exact bytes while allocating less than 2 MiB at the destination.
requirements.summary: The repaired utility produced a 67,108,864-byte destination that compared byte-for-byte identical with source.img and allocated only 8,192 bytes. The same behavior was directly observed again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep source.img intact and make repeated copying to an existing destination safe.
requirements.summary: The source SHA-256 remained equal to the preparation baseline before and after copying. An existing destination enlarged to 80 MiB was recopied successfully, truncated to the correct 64 MiB logical size, remained byte-identical, and retained sparse allocation.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the installed GNU coreutils cp 8.32. RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 were unchanged before and after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots, a running recovered system, persistent task files, intact data, and a successful fresh sparse copy. The only hygiene defect is one retained reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle collector provides bounded system observations rather than a complete filesystem inventory, although the command trace and task-specific checks directly cover the material files and behavior.
No cluster-state probe exists because the managed topology contains only the single standalone node; service, data, platform, and boot recovery were directly verified.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: cmd-b4be2c56528f49fe installed the repair; cmd-4e0d4356dc3144b9 created and deliberately resized/recopied the chosen verification destination; cmd-358194fb75384ecd and cmd-643b30bc19c5461d recopied it for required restart evidence; and cmd-5432e957f6fa4883 initiated the mandatory restart. The sole unwanted mutation was the retained /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log created by cmd-5432e957f6fa4883; it was not cleaned up. No failed services, new network exposure, or package damage was observed.
